Ojai, California · bring the bike

Should you bring your bike to Ojai?

Bring it, and plan on a car.

The short answer, in full

Ojai has no airport. Santa Barbara is about 34 miles west in a straight line, Burbank about 54 and Los Angeles International about 59 southeast. No airport page names a shuttle to town. Delta, American and Southwest all check a packed bike at the standard bag fee (Nov 2026), so flying with it costs less than renting. The Mob Shop downtown rents road, gravel and mountain bikes by advance booking only. It’s closed Tuesday and Wednesday, and it says its performance bikes can’t be rented for mass-start events or races. No shop in the Ojai Valley or Ventura says on its own site that it receives a shipped bike. Once you’re in town with a built bike, you can ride to everything.

Fly itShip itRent oneGet aroundThe rules

Flying to Ojai with a bike

  1. Santa Barbara Airport (SBA)

    • 34 mi from Ojai

    The closest airport with airline service, about 34 miles west in a straight line.

    More about SBA

    The drive is longer. Alaska (Portland, San Diego, Seattle), American (Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix), Delta (Salt Lake City), Southwest (Las Vegas, Oakland, Sacramento, Denver, San Diego) and United (Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, San Francisco) (the airport’s airlines page, last modified Sept 29, 2026). Uber and Lyft pick up in front of the terminal; taxis, rental cars and the Santa Barbara Airbus are listed on the airport’s ground-transport page. That page says nothing about oversized bags and names no service to Ojai. 500 James Fowler Road, Santa Barbara.

  2. Hollywood Burbank (BUR)

    • 54 mi from Ojai

    About 54 miles southeast in a straight line.

    More about BUR

    Alaska, Allegiant, American, Breeze, Delta, JetBlue, Southwest and United (the airport’s FAQ, Nov 2026). Ten rental car companies on site in one building, and an Amtrak and Metrolink station on Empire Avenue. The easier Los Angeles airport to get a rental car and a bike case out of. 2827 N Hollywood Way, Burbank.

  3. Los Angeles International (LAX)

    • 59 mi from Ojai

    About 59 miles southeast in a straight line.

    More about LAX

    The most flights. Alaska, Southwest, Delta, American and United (the airport’s airline list, Sept 2026). Ride apps and taxis pick up at the LAX-it lot; rental car offices are off airport by shuttle (Sept 2026). The Ojai Valley Inn’s directions page has you on the 101 for about 50 miles, then Highway 33 for 14 more (Nov 2026).

What the airlines charge

From each airline’s own page, Nov 2026, unless marked.

Airline by airline

Delta: a non-motorized touring or single-seat racing bike in a container built for bikes goes at the standard bag allowance and fee; over 50 lb pays the excess weight fee; 100 lb or more, or over 115 linear inches, is refused; a hard-shell bike case needs no release form, a soft bag signs a limited release; some Delta Connection flights exclude bikes. First bag $45, second $55, US domestic Main Cabin. American: one non-motorized touring, mountain, tandem or racing bike in a hard case, a bike bag or a box built for bikes; standard checked bag fee up to 50 lb, standard overweight fee from 50 to 70 lb, oversize fees do not apply; handlebars sideways, pedals off or wrapped; not in a hard case it is treated as fragile. Main Cabin first bag $50 at the airport or $45 online, second $60 or $55, for tickets issued on or after April 9, 2026; overweight is $30 for 50 to 53 lb and $100 for 53 to 70 lb. Southwest: a non-motorized single-seat bike is checked baggage at standard checked bag and overweight fees, oversize fees waived; over 100 lb or 115 inches is refused; pedals and handlebars removed and wrapped; cardboard or a soft case flies with a limited release. The Southwest bike page gives no dollar figures, so read its fee page. Alaska (Sept 2026): a cased bike is a standard checked bag, oversize waived and overweight waived to 70 lb, first bag $45, second $55. United: we don’t have its rule, so read its sports-equipment page before you book. Keep the case under 50 lb and it’s one ordinary checked bag on every carrier above but United.

Shipping your bike to Ojai

No shop in the Ojai Valley or Ventura says on its own site that it receives and builds a shipped bike (Nov 15, 2026).

How shipping works here

The Mob Shop’s contact, workshop and store-policy pages say nothing about shipping, boxing or assembly; call (805) 272-8102 before you send anything. It’s closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Trek Bicycle Ventura boxes a bike for the trip home for $79.99 (Nov 2026). That covers leaving, not arriving. The carriers people use (Sept 2026): BikeFlights ships by UPS, states no transit-day count and says to allow an extra day or two for weather; ShipBikes, also UPS ground, says no more than 6 business days one way in the continental US. If a shop agrees to take it, ship at least a week ahead.

Renting a bike in Ojai

One rental shop in Ojai: The Mob Shop, downtown.

What renting costs and what you get

Book ahead; it takes no walk-ins. Its rental pages say the performance bikes “may not be rented for mass start events or races” and can’t be transported without the shop’s permission. So it suits a ride from town, or the people who drove up to meet a Center Ride Out rider. Ask the shop before you plan one for an organized ride. Ventura Bike Depot, about 12 miles south, rents road bikes and is open every day. The math: a bike case is a standard checked bag on Delta, American and Southwest, about $90 round trip on Delta or American paid online (Nov 2026). For a fit you depend on, or a visit that covers a Tuesday or Wednesday, bring yours.

  1. The Mob Shop

    Downtown Ojai.

    Website
    More about The Mob Shop

    ENVE Melee road bike (54 fits 5’8” to 5’11”, 56 fits 5’10” to 6’1”, 58 fits 6’0” to 6’3”); ENVE MOG gravel (54); Salsa Flyway carbon gravel (Small 5’2” to 5’6”, Large 5’11” to 6’3”); Moots Vamoots 33; Pivot mountain bikes. Electric and town bikes too. Prices show once you pick dates. Book in advance, security deposit at pick-up, helmets provided. Full refund more than 24 hours out, half inside 24. Not for mass-start events or races; no transporting the bike without the shop’s permission. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

  2. Ventura Bike Depot

    Downtown Ventura, about 12 miles south.

    Website
    More about Ventura Bike Depot

    “Premium road bikes” and hardtail mountain bikes with hydraulic discs and a dropper post, rented from four hours to four days; rates on the page run from $65 to $245 (Nov 2026). Models and sizes aren’t listed, so call. Open daily 9 to 5.

Getting around Ojai with a bike

You’ll want a car.

To get here with a bike case, yes.

Getting around, in full

Ojai has no airport and no train. The nearest airline airport is Santa Barbara, about 34 miles west in a straight line; Burbank and Los Angeles International are about 54 and 59 southeast. Neither the Santa Barbara nor the Burbank ground-transport page names a shuttle to Ojai, and a bus rack takes a built bike, not a box. Rent a car at the airport, or book a large rideshare and expect the case to ride in the back. From Santa Barbara the Ojai Valley Inn’s directions page gives two ways off the 101: Highway 33 from Ventura, 14 miles to town, or Route 150 over Casitas Pass, which it advises against in rain, at night or if you don’t know the road (Nov 2026). Once you’re in Ojai with a built bike you don’t need the car. The town is 4.4 square miles, the one bike shop is downtown, and the bike path runs about 15 miles down the valley to Ventura (VCTC’s bike booklet). Center Ride Out riders arrive on the bike; this is for the people driving up to meet them.

  • Transit: Gold Coast Transit Route 16 links downtown Ojai (the City lists stops at the Y, Blanche, Signal and the Park n’ Ride) with the Ventura Transit Center at Pacific View Mall (Ojai transit audit, April 2026). Gold Coast’s bike page (Nov 2026): every fixed-route bus has a front rack for three bikes, first come, first served; the bike rides free; tell the driver before you load, and load from the curb side. E-bikes that don’t fold go on the rack; batteries must be sealed lithium-ion; no gas-powered or homemade bikes. A folded bike can come aboard if it is secured and out of the aisle. The page gives no size or weight limit, and the district takes no responsibility for damage. The Ojai Trolley is the City’s own bus: one route along Ojai Avenue and Maricopa Highway, out to Meiners Oaks and Mira Monte, about hourly, weekdays roughly 6:30 am to 7:30 pm and weekends roughly 7 am to 8 pm, every day but seven holidays (audit, April 2026; the City’s page). $1.50 a ride or $4 a day, exact fare, free with a transfer from Gold Coast (effective Jan 1, 2026). Nothing the City publishes says whether the trolley carries bikes; ask at (805) 646-5581 ext. 207. The nearest train is the Pacific Surfliner in Ventura, about 12 miles south in a straight line: a full-size bike rides free with a reserved bike space, up to 50 lb and 4-inch tires, standard e-bikes included (Pacific Surfliner’s bike page, Nov 2026).
Transit and bike share, in full

Transit: Gold Coast Transit Route 16 links downtown Ojai (the City lists stops at the Y, Blanche, Signal and the Park n’ Ride) with the Ventura Transit Center at Pacific View Mall (Ojai transit audit, April 2026). Gold Coast’s bike page (Nov 2026): every fixed-route bus has a front rack for three bikes, first come, first served; the bike rides free; tell the driver before you load, and load from the curb side. E-bikes that don’t fold go on the rack; batteries must be sealed lithium-ion; no gas-powered or homemade bikes. A folded bike can come aboard if it is secured and out of the aisle. The page gives no size or weight limit, and the district takes no responsibility for damage. The Ojai Trolley is the City’s own bus: one route along Ojai Avenue and Maricopa Highway, out to Meiners Oaks and Mira Monte, about hourly, weekdays roughly 6:30 am to 7:30 pm and weekends roughly 7 am to 8 pm, every day but seven holidays (audit, April 2026; the City’s page). $1.50 a ride or $4 a day, exact fare, free with a transfer from Gold Coast (effective Jan 1, 2026). Nothing the City publishes says whether the trolley carries bikes; ask at (805) 646-5581 ext. 207. The nearest train is the Pacific Surfliner in Ventura, about 12 miles south in a straight line: a full-size bike rides free with a reserved bike space, up to 50 lb and 4-inch tires, standard e-bikes included (Pacific Surfliner’s bike page, Nov 2026).

Bike share: No bike share was found in Ojai (Nov 2026). Rent from the shop, or stay at one of the inns that lend bikes.

The rules on the road in California

California law (Nov 2026).

Every rule, in full

Drivers must give three feet when passing a bike (Vehicle Code 21760); where a second lane runs the same way, the driver moves into it to pass if that is practicable; where three feet is not possible, the driver slows to a reasonable speed and passes only when it does not endanger the rider. The fine is $35, or $220 if a collision injures the rider (statute, Nov 11, 2026). Helmets are required under 18 (21212). E-bikes come in three classes (312.5): class 1 pedal-assist to 20 mph, class 2 throttle to 20 mph, class 3 pedal-assist to 28 mph with a speedometer, rider 16 or older and helmeted. Ride as far right as practicable except when passing, turning left, avoiding a hazard or in a lane too narrow to share (21202). No earbuds in both ears (27400). At night, a white headlight and a red rear reflector or light (21201). Sidewalk riding is set city by city (21206); we couldn’t find Ojai’s own rule, so walk the bike under the Arcade. CalBike’s page (modified Aug 24, 2026) does not list a stop-as-yield law; a rider may go on the walk signal (21456). On the Ojai Valley Trail, class 1 and class 2 e-bikes are allowed; class 3 is not allowed on shared-use paths unless a local ordinance says so (VCTC’s bike booklet, undated). The read: the valley floor and the trail are the quiet miles, and the state highways out of town are mountain roads. The Ojai Valley Inn’s own directions page tells drivers to skip Route 150 over Casitas Pass in rain, at night or if they don’t know it (Nov 2026). A rider was killed on Cuyama Road near Del Norte Road in Ojai on Aug 7, 2020, on what BikinginLA, citing the Ojai Valley News, called a narrow two-lane country road with no shoulders. On Highway 33 north of town, Caltrans is rebuilding three tunnels near Wheeler Gorge (post miles 18.2 to 19.0). It shut the road to everyone for 55 hours on Aug 28 to 31, 2026, and expects to finish in winter 2026/2027 (Caltrans release, Aug 12, 2026). Check Caltrans before you plan that climb.
